motion: Longevity science could extend your healthspan by decades, and the government should fund it.

dropped_turns.text: You call access a reason to spend, but spending first does not make a treatment work or reach anyone. Your example assumes success, while the motion asks taxpayers to fund uncertain decades-long promises; reject it.

dropped_turns.text: Picture a caregiver who can keep lifting groceries and walking outside because a publicly developed treatment delayed weakness. That extra healthy decade means less dependence and more choice, proving public funding deserves support.

turns.text: Private insurers may change premiums when people live longer, and families may rethink retirement. But those are later questions; the motion asks whether public research can protect healthy years, and it can.

turns.speaker: PRO

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: No, people should not wait for perfect certainty before seeking care. But your gamble premise fails: transparent public trials reduce uncertainty and give everyone access, which is precisely why the government should fund this.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: If private sellers control these therapies, how will a worker with little savings receive them before disability arrives? Your plan assumes access follows discovery, but public funding is not the answer, so oppose it.
